llm.summary: The skill's behavior (downloading a GitHub repo, creating a virtualenv, and requiring an LLM API key) is consistent with its stated purpose, but there are several mismatches and transparency gaps you should be aware of before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (fetch and summarize arXiv/HuggingFace papers) matches the included scripts and SKILL.md. However the registry metadata declares no required env vars while the SKILL.md explicitly requires an LLM key (SKILLBOSS_API_KEY). README also references a different GitHub repo path than the bootstrap script (ModestyRichards vs matanle51), which is an inconsistency worth checking.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are explicit: bootstrap (clone/download repo), create virtualenv, pip install requirements, source a .env, run CLI/API, and read/modify config files under PROJECT_DIR. These actions are within scope for a paper-digest tool. The SKILL.md mandates the agent open and read repo config files and prompt the user to edit them — that requires access to files in PROJECT_DIR and to an LLM API key. The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated system files or transmit secrets to unexpected endpoints, but the agent will load .env which may contain sensitive values.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec in registry, but bootstrap.sh downloads the code from GitHub (https://github.com/matanle51/agentic_paper_digest) or clones via git, extracts it, and pip-installs requirements.txt. Using GitHub releases/zip is typical and lower risk than arbitrary servers, but pip install of repo requirements can pull arbitrary PyPI packages — inspect requirements.txt before running. The mismatch in README repo URL is another minor red flag to confirm origin.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill legitimately needs an LLM API key (SKILLBOSS_API_KEY) to run summarization via the SkillBoss hub. However the registry metadata did not declare this required environment variable, which is a transparency gap. The scripts will also load a .env file and export keys into LITELLM_API_KEY/LITELLM_API_BASE, so any secrets in .env will be used. No unrelated cloud credentials or other service tokens are requested, so the scope of secrets is proportional — but verify the missing registry declaration and double-check any .env content before use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal agent invocation are used. The skill writes to PROJECT_DIR, creates a .venv, and may create a .env from .env.example — all confined to the project folder. It does not request global agent privileges or modify other skills. Stopping is via simple scripts. This is typical for a local tool.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing: 1) Confirm the repository author and URL — bootstrap.sh clones https://github.com/matanle51/agentic_paper_digest, but README mentions a different repo; make sure you intended to use the correct upstream. 2) Inspect the repository you will download, especially requirements.txt and any code that runs network calls, before running bootstrap.sh or pip installing. 3) Treat SKILLBOSS_API_KEY as sensitive: only provide a key you trust and prefer a least-privilege/test account; the scripts map it into LITELLM_API_KEY and the tool will send requests to the SkillBoss hub. 4) Run the tool in an isolated environment (container or VM) if you want to limit blast radius from pip packages or remote code. 5) Review PROJECT_DIR/.env for other secrets before bootstrap or set ENV_FILE to a safe file. 6) If you are unsure about the upstream owner or requirements, ask the skill author for clarity or prefer manual installation after code review.
